questions.question: Discuss the techniques and significance of somatic hybridization and cybridization.
questions.solution_html:
• A: Somatic hybridization and cybridization are biotechnological techniques that enable the
  • combination of genetic material from different plant species, overcoming barriers of sexual
  • incompatibility.
  • This method fuses protoplasts—plant cells without cell walls—from two species to form a hybrid
  • containing both nuclear and cytoplasmic genomes.
  • Technique: Protoplasts are first isolated by enzymatically removing cell walls using cellulase and
  • pectinase. The protoplasts are then cultured in a nutrient medium and fused using chemical agents like
  • polyethylene glycol (PEG) or electrical pulses. Hybrid cells are selected through metabolic markers or
  • fluorescence and regenerated into whole plants.
  • Significance: Somatic hybridization enables the creation of novel genetic combinations which are not
  • possible through sexual crosses, including interspecific or intergeneric hybrids. It can produce fertile
  • plants from sterile parents and introduce valuable cytoplasmic traits like disease resistance or stress
  • tolerance. Applications include developing disease-resistant Citrus varieties and improving fruit
  • quality in persimmons.
  • Cybridization
  • Cybridization, or cytoplasmic hybridization, involves the fusion of a whole protoplast from one parent
  • with an enucleated protoplast (cytoplast) from another. The resulting cybrid carries the nuclear
  • genome of one species and the cytoplasm of both.
  • Technique: One parent’s cells are enucleated, and these cytoplasts are fused with intact donor
  • protoplasts. The resulting cells are cultured and regenerated into plants.
  • Significance: Cybridization allows selective transfer of cytoplasmic traits—such as cytoplasmic male
  • sterility, herbicide tolerance, or disease resistance—without altering the nuclear genome. It is
  • particularly useful in breeding programs to introduce desirable cytoplasmic characteristics while
  • retaining the superior nuclear background of a cultivar.

questions.final_answer: retaining the superior nuclear background of a cultivar.
